Riding your bike with no handlebars is pretty useful if you want to add or remove layers of clothing or perform any other task requiring two-handed dexterity without stopping. That said, it can be a two edged sword. It's dangerous to attempt while in the flow of traffic, going downhill, going too slow, with traffic passing you to one side, with pedestrians around, while you're in a door zone, or while riding a bike that's not in good condition, so be careful. Your response time is reduced while your hands are off the bars, so practice and perform this technique only under safe conditions.

Having just recently gained some confidence with this ability myself, I thought I'd share a few tips on how to learn it. First off, start with one hand. That's pretty easy. Keep pedaling and sit upright so you can lean back and put your weight over the rear wheel. Take your remaining hand off the bars for short intervals. Keep practicing this until you can confidently do it for longer and longer periods of time. Steer the bike with your hips, making small adjustments and taking care not to overcompensate. If you start to wobble, grab the bars.

That's pretty much it. If you practice this regularly, you'll probably get better at it without even having to think about it. Your body will just kind of learn it reflexively, if that makes sense to you.

If you have a bike which can accommodate a front stabilizer, you might consider getting one. It's a spring that clamps onto your downtube and bolts into the back of the fork crown, keeping your bike's front end more stable while still allowing you to easily turn the front wheel when you want. It's a pretty common accessory on dutch bikes and you will sometimes see them on touring bikes, and it could be very helpful in learning how to ride with your hands off the bars. It helped me a lot, and now I can do it on my road bike which doesn't have a stabilizer. Your local bike shop may not carry one, so in that case you'd have to order it.

Here's a video outlining a slightly different method of learning the technique which some people may find easier: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Sm9j0S_dCZ0
